title: Concurrent multi-domain security of tweaked-SR
summary: Prove concurrent security of tweaked-SR when its round constants do not encode the initial domain.

formal_statement.body: Let the initial domain size $N_0$ range over arbitrary positive integers. In tweaked-SR, allow the round functions to remain domain-separated by $N_0$, but choose each round constant $K(i,N)$ using only the round index $i$ and current recursive domain size $N$, independently of $N_0$. Prove that the resulting family is secure in the source multi-slice PRP game against every finite adversary making concurrent queries across arbitrary initial domains, or give a compatible adversary that refutes this claim.

scope.domain: The tweaked Sometimes-Recurse format-preserving permutation family over arbitrary finite initial domains
assumptions: Round functions may remain separated by the initial domain N0
Round constants depend only on the current recursive size N and round index i
The adversary may query several initial domains concurrently
Security is measured in the source multi-slice PRP experiment
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later result proves or refutes concurrent multi-domain security for tweaked-SR under the exact restriction that round constants omit N0 while round functions may retain domain separation.

provenance.note: The first archived ePrint version dated September 4, 2013 already contains the conjecture. The cited 2009 multi-slice PRP definition supplies the security game but does not state the tweaked-SR question.

citations.label: Morris--Rogaway, Sometimes-Recurse multi-domain conjecture
citations.locator: First archived ePrint version, final discussion, 'Multiple concurrent domains'; revised version, p. 14

progress.summary: The first archived ePrint version conjectures that tweaked-SR remains concurrently secure across arbitrary initial domains when round constants omit the initial domain identifier.
